claim: Chemingui et al. 2024 (PG-GS) explicitly assert, in their own Summary/Future Work section, that prior offline BBO methods focused on improving surrogate models while using fixed search strategies -- confirming the falsification-target premise the audited paper attributes to this source.
stance_target: Audited paper's claim that it falsifies 'the local premise of one recent paper -- that offline black-box optimization has focused on improving surrogate models while using fixed search strategies (chemingui2024pggs)'
scope_conditions: Summary and Future Work section of Chemingui et al., AAAI 2024
quoted_support: This perspective is aimed at improving the search strategy in offline BBO, which complements prior methods that have focused on improving surrogate models while using fixed search strategies.

claim: Chemingui et al.'s Related Work section names the specific prior methods it characterizes as fixed-search-strategy-with-improving-surrogate: Trabucco et al. 2021 (COMs), Yu et al. 2021a, and Fu and Levine 2021.
stance_target: Precision of the falsification-target premise -- is it a claim about the whole field or specific named prior works?
scope_conditions: Related Work section, second family of offline optimization methods
quoted_support: The second family learns a surrogate model from the offline data which is then optimized directly using gradient updates (Trabucco et al. 2021; Yu et al. 2021a; Fu and Levine 2021). Conservative regularizers are typically designed to avoid overestimation for inputs which are far away from the offline training data.

claim: Chemingui et al.'s abstract itself states the same premise in slightly different words, describing prior approaches' search strategies as 'derived from the surrogate model rather than the actual offline data' -- a second, independent verbatim confirmation.
stance_target: Robustness of the falsification-target premise attribution
quoted_support: Prior approaches addressing this challenge have primarily focused on learning robust surrogate models. However, their search strategies are derived from the surrogate model rather than the actual offline data.

claim: PG-GS reformulates offline optimization as an offline RL problem, learning a policy that outputs a direction vector to replace the fixed step-size in a standard gradient update, explicitly to correct for non-smooth/sub-optimal surrogate gradients.
stance_target: Mechanism description for accurate characterization of what PG-GS actually changes
quoted_support: The key idea behind PGS is to reformulate the step-size in the standard gradient update into a direction vector. Such direction vector can be viewed as an output alpha = pi(x_k) of a guiding policy pi to direct the search space exploration from x_k in the direction of the high-performing input regions.

claim: PG-GS is evaluated on Design-Bench tasks (Trabucco et al. 2022), establishing Design-Bench as the shared empirical substrate across this offline-MBO evaluation surface.
stance_target: Cross-referencing the evaluation benchmark landscape for the N6 kill-surface check
quoted_support: Empirical evaluation on diverse optimization tasks from the design-bench benchmark (Trabucco et al. 2022) demonstrates that PGS performs better than prior methods on many tasks.
